rationale: Empirical prober (claude substitute for the refused codex slot). Everything I could measure, I measured against the real code at 482bcd2f: (1) all 21 TestBead6Leg fixture legs PASS (-short, run twice; the twenty named legs plus viii-a); (2) all 11 ADR-0041 pinning tests PASS, including the red-if-old-sentence pin TestADR0041OQ1a_OldGatesAfterCommitClaimGone; (3) I built the mindspec binary from the reviewed commit and hand-drove the FLAGSHIP scenario in a scratch fixture (flat layout, real git worktrees, stateful fake bd on PATH, a 6/6-APPROVE panel registered at SHA A in the spec worktree's spec dir): with a clean bead worktree whose tip A carries a source-only change, `complete` REFUSED at doc-sync and left the bead tip EXACTLY at A (byte-equal SHA), zero refs/mindspec/* markers, no complete-authored commit anywhere — the #186 regression probe holds; a plain retry met the IDENTICAL doc-sync gate (no false panel-staleness); the `--allow-doc-skew` retry let the same gate class decide, recorded mindspec_doc_skew_reason/by/at in bead metadata, correctly ELIDED both C and D (snapshot tree == tip tree; merge second parent IS A — reviewed SHA == landing commit, the #186/#233 coupling promise), merged into the spec branch, closed the bead, removed the worktree, and left zero markers (T). In a second fixture variant with uncommitted prospective dirt I also drove the MATERIALIZING path end-to-end: C = 'mindspec: materialize bead completion' with the Mindspec-Stage: materialization trailer, parent exactly A, containing the prospective edit; D elided; merge landed; marker cleared. (4) AC-7(i) verified live: a foreign non-tracker commit after panel registration trips the stale-SHA panel BLOCK (with the raw-merge fence text) BEFORE any content gate, tip unmoved. (5) Bonus honesty observed: with a live panel and uncommitted worktree changes, the panel gate refuses ('would auto-commit them past review') rather than laundering dirt past the reviewed SHA. So the bead's headline guarantees are real and I could not break the marker/CAS/elision machinery from outside. HOWEVER, deviation C's window is empirically OPEN (finding R4-F1, MAJOR): a mutation landing between the pre-S dirt classification (materialize.go:276) and the S-stage add -A snapshot (materialize.go:292, exclude=nil) is SILENTLY SWEPT into the artifact-sync commit D, and the S-exit re-check is structurally blind to it (after the D advance + index reset the worktree is clean — its own doc comment admits it is 'not expected to find anything NEW'). I reproduced this with a decorator executor injecting a worktree write at the start of the second SnapshotWorktreeTree call: Run returned SUCCESS, BeadClosed, and the injected non-artifact file exists at the final bead tip — ungated, unpaneled content committed and mergeable, violating the plan's own invariant ('an interval edit is preserved on disk behind a named refusal or an explicitly safe recovery' / legs' 'never silent loss'). The injection is timing-equivalent to an external writer (an editor flush, a concurrent agent) — no privileged seam is involved. The fix is small and TOTAL because the data is already in hand: D's own delta (changedFromCurrent) is computed at materialize.go:296 — refusing when it contains any non-artifact path classifies the EXACT tree being committed, eliminating the TOCTOU on both the normal and resume routes. With that gate, deviation B (D via full re-snapshot) becomes genuinely safe; without it, B is exactly the coupling that makes the sweep possible. Deviation A I observed empirically (the operator's message appears nowhere in the landed history) — acceptable as disclosed, recommendation only. Secondary (R4-F2, MINOR): ADR-0041 §3(i) still describes the PLAN's ordering ('S — build commit D ..., then the S-exit dirt contract') and nowhere mentions the delivered classification-BEFORE-the-snapshot — the BRIEF's own question 'does the doc describe what ships?' answers no. Conduct disclosures: the bead worktree contained an untracked leftover reproducer (internal/complete/r4_pres_snapshot_race_probe_test.go, evidently from the refused codex R4 session); I verified its premise independently against the code path before running it, ran it (PASS = race reproduced, logged 'RACE_REPRODUCED ... non-artifact edit silently committed by D'), captured its approach in R4-F1's repro recipe, then DELETED it to restore the worktree byte-identical with 482bcd2f (git status clean, full internal/complete -short suite re-run green, 'ok ... 56.380s'). All scratch fixtures under the session scratchpad were removed.
concrete_changes_required: R4-F1 (MAJOR): Close the pre-S classification→snapshot race in runMaterialization (internal/complete/materialize.go). After computing changedFromCurrent (line ~296), REFUSE (named paths, sExitGenuineDirtRefusal-style, before MaterializeStageCommit) if any path in D's delta is outside materializedArtifactPaths — this classifies the exact tree2 being committed, closing the TOCTOU totally on BOTH the normal route and the resumeStage==stageMaterialization route. Add a fixture leg pinning it: a decorator executor that writes a non-artifact file into the bead worktree at the start of the SECOND SnapshotWorktreeTree call must produce a REFUSAL naming the path (edit preserved on disk, tip not advanced past C), never a commit containing it. Repro recipe (verified at 482bcd2f, currently completes successfully with the file at the final tip): wrap the real executor, count SnapshotWorktreeTree calls, on call 2 write race-file.txt into wtPath before delegating; drive Run via the leg-fixture harness (setupRealGitFaultFixture + wireRealGitFaultSeams + wireBeadWorktree, commitMsg set, pre-seeded artifact dirt); assert the run refuses instead of closing.

R4-F2 (MINOR): ADR-0041 §3(i) (and §1's S bullet) must describe the DELIVERED ordering — the interval-edit classification runs BEFORE the S-stage snapshot, with the S-exit contract as a defensive re-check — instead of the plan's original check-after-D wording ('S — build commit D ..., then the S-exit dirt contract'). Extend/adjust the pinning tests so the delivered ordering is the pinned one (and, if R4-F1 lands, describe the delta-classification gate as the primary enforcement point).

findings.title: Deviation C's window is open: a mutation between the pre-S classification and the S snapshot is silently committed into D, blinding the S-exit re-check
findings.detail: Empirically reproduced at 482bcd2f: injecting a non-artifact worktree write at the start of the second SnapshotWorktreeTree call (timing-equivalent to an external editor/agent write in the interval between checkDirtyTreeFn at materialize.go:276 and the add -A snapshot at materialize.go:292) yields a SUCCESSFUL complete with BeadClosed and the injected file present in the final bead tip's tree — swept into the stage-named artifact-sync commit D, ungated (doc-sync/ADR ran on the earlier M snapshot) and unpaneled. The S-exit contract cannot catch it: after the D branch-advance and ResetIndexToHead the worktree is clean, so both the re-check and any operator inspection see nothing. This violates the plan's invariant that an interval edit is 'preserved on disk behind a named refusal or an explicitly safe recovery', never silently committed. The window is narrow (in-process, between two adjacent steps) but this bead's entire subject is refusing to launder unreviewed state, and the total fix is one comparison over data already computed: refuse when changedFromCurrent contains any non-artifact path (see concrete change 1). Deviation B (full re-snapshot with exclude=nil) is judged acceptable ONLY together with that gate — as delivered, B is what makes the sweep expressible.

findings.title: ADR-0041 does not describe deviation C's delivered ordering
findings.detail: §3(i)'s S bullet reads 'build commit D ..., then the S-exit dirt contract' and §1 speaks only of 'a final S-exit dirt re-classification' — the plan's original check-after-D ordering. The delivered, load-bearing check runs BEFORE the D snapshot (materialize.go:276), with the exit contract demoted to a defensive re-confirmation. Grep confirms no ADR text mentions the pre-snapshot classification. The BRIEF's deviation-C question 'does the ADR §3(i) text describe the delivered ordering?' — it does not.

findings.title: Deviation A observed empirically: the operator's commit message vanishes from the audit trail entirely
findings.detail: In the materializing flagship run with commitMsg 'flagship work', that string appears nowhere in the landed history — C's subject is the fixed 'mindspec: materialize bead completion' with only the Mindspec-Stage trailer. Disclosed and cosmetically acceptable (the doc-skew override reason IS durably recorded in bd metadata), but the message could be preserved as a body line of C at zero protocol cost. Recommendation only, not a required change.

findings.title: Positive empirical results: legs, ADR pins, flagship, #186 probe, AC-7(i), panel-dirt honesty
findings.detail: 21/21 TestBead6Leg PASS (-short); 11/11 ADR-0041 pinning tests PASS including the red-if-old-sentence pin. Real-binary flagship (scratch fixture, live 6/6 panel at SHA A in the spec worktree): doc-sync refusal left tip byte-equal to A with zero refs/mindspec/* markers; plain retry met the identical gate (no staleness false-fire); --allow-doc-skew retry converged with C and D both correctly elided — the merge's second parent IS the reviewed SHA A — then close, worktree removal, marker clear, and mindspec_doc_skew_* + mindspec_landed_* metadata writes, in order. Materializing variant verified separately: C carries 'Mindspec-Stage: materialization', parent exactly A, prospective content included; D elided; merge landed; markers cleared. AC-7(i): a foreign non-tracker commit after registration trips the stale-SHA panel BLOCK (with the raw-merge fence) BEFORE any content gate, tip unmoved. With a live panel, uncommitted worktree changes refuse at the panel gate ('would auto-commit them past review') rather than laundering dirt past the reviewed SHA. Fixture-methodology note for other reviewers: the panel must live under the SPEC WORKTREE's spec dir — workspace.SpecDir prefers .worktrees/worktree-spec-<id>/.mindspec/specs/<id> over the root copy, and a root-only panel silently fail-opens the gate (production layouts, like this repo's, put panels in the spec worktree, so this is fixture placement, not a code bug — but the silent fail-open's UX may deserve a doctor-level surfacing someday).
